text:
Erin: Starting a staged traffic cutover for v3.4.0 — canary at 5% — seeing errors from model-serving pods in eu-west-1 immediately after shift. Observability shows failed connections to redis and upstream KV store. Anyone else seeing this?
Jamal: I see a cluster-wide spike in TCP CLOSE_WAIT and restarts on nodegroup-ml-eu-1. Pods are getting PLEG / eviction warnings.
Sasha: deploy-bot reported canary rollout status: FAILED -> stalled at traffic split. It also auto-attenuated to 1% but errors persisted.
deploy-bot: [deploy] rollout v3.4.0 canary: 5% -> alert: pod-health-check-failure (svc/model-svc)
Raj: paste of `kubectl top nodes` and `ss -s` attached — node conntrack tables look saturated. SNAT connections are being reused aggressively.
Clement: hmm, might be conntrack exhaustion on the bottleneck NAT nodes. We recently bumped max pods per node in that nodepool; more pods => more ephemeral connections per node.
Erin: logs from one failing pod: `dial tcp 10.100.2.12:6379: connect: connection refused` then `context deadline exceeded`. No obvious app-level bugs yet.
Sasha: can we quickly raise `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` via a DaemonSet sysctl init? That would be faster than scaling nodepool.
Jamal: we tried a quick patch on one node (sysctl write) and connections recovered for a minute then other limits (SNAT ports) hit. Looks like SNAT port exhaustion on the NAT gateway nodepool.
Raj: ops-bot metrics show SNAT port usage near 64000 per NAT node. We're running out of ephemeral ports because kube-proxy + hostSNAT mix is high.
Clement: two mitigation paths: 1) roll back traffic to 0% (fast), 2) scale dedicated NAT nodepool and add NAT ip pools / egress nodes (slower + cost). Recommendation: rollback canary while we patch networking.
Erin: agree with rollback. How do we trigger fast rollback with GitOps? deploy-bot, can you revert the staged-split PR?
deploy-bot: To revert: `gh pr revert 4321 --body "rollback: canary conntrack/SNAT issue"` then push — GitOps controller will sync and route to previous weights.
Sasha: I'll open the revert PR now and patch a short-term kubelet sysctl DaemonSet and a change to ingress egress annotation to prefer distributed egress IPs.
Jamal: also adding `tcp_tw_reuse=1` isn't ideal but could reduce TIME_WAIT churn. Put that behind a nodepool feature flag.
Raj: logging note — capture `conntrack -L | wc -l` and `ss -s` snapshots; saved to /tmp/conntrack-dump-{{ts}}. We need these for postmortem and to tune autotune rules.
Clement: long term: consider eBPF-based conntrack offload and dedicated egress proxies to avoid host SNAT hot spots. But that's a multi-week project.
Erin: OK rollback PR up at https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/ - PR 4330 revert. I've also paged infra on-call to scale temporary nat nodes if rollback doesn't cut 0->100%.
Raj: on-call confirmed they can add two extra NAT nodes in eu-west-1; but cost estimate ~ $1.8k/day while active.
Sasha: for CI/CD hygiene: we should add a pre-cutover smoke test that simulates high connection churn (short-lived TCP clients) against the cluster before shifting more than 5%. That would've caught this.
Erin: good call — adding a staged gate to the release workflow. For now let's watch after revert and keep canary at 0%.
Clement: postmortem owners: Erin (lead), Raj (network), Sasha (release pipeline). I'll file an incident doc and add a follow-up RFC for egress architecture. :spiral_note_pad:
Erin: thanks all. moving to rollback and monitoring.
